one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled event falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29: FY27 Q1 earnings historically land in the second half of November, and Investor Day (Sep 17) already reaffirmed Q1 and FY27 guidance. Minor in-window items: Xero's US price increase on Oct 1 (narrows the QuickBooks price gap slightly, marginal), QuickBooks renewals at the new August price points, and continuing news flow on AI tax/bookkeeping agents. Short-horizon regularities conflict: the stock fell ~23% in the past month to near its 52-week low (momentum negative, but sharp-drop reversal is also common). With no scheduled catalyst I stay close to a symmetric lognormal centred on $268 using monthly vol ~14% (50%/3.5).

bear.story: Tax season 2027 (TY2026) shows TurboTax unit share loss to FreeTaxUSA/AI agents (Perplexity, TaxGPT, Instead), QuickBooks price hikes of 20-40% trigger visible churn, FY28 guide implies high-single-digit growth at best; multiple compresses to ~8x ~$22-23 EPS.

base.story: FY27 delivered roughly to guide (~$23 EPS), TurboTax flat-ish units with Live/assisted growth, QBO pricing sticks with modest churn, big buybacks shrink share count; AI-disruption discount persists and stock trades ~11.5-12x FY28 EPS ~$26.

bull.story: Tax season proves resilient (agents integrate with rather than replace TurboTax; Direct File stays suspended), Intuit Enterprise Suite and mid-market scale, customer growth re-accelerates; multiple recovers to ~16-17x FY28 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$190 the stock would sit near 8x guided FY27 EPS and ~12%+ SBC-adjusted FCF yield, a level that only makes sense if the market is pricing an actual earnings decline (lost TurboTax units in the 2027 season, QuickBooks churn after price hikes, or a guide cut), not just sentiment. It is also ~25% below the current 52-week low of $252.84, beyond ordinary volatility after a 60% drawdown.

reasoning: Facts: FY26 revenue $21.4B (+14%), non-GAAP EPS $24.27, FCF ~$8.6B; FY27 guide revenue +9-10%, non-GAAP EPS $22.88-23.12 now including SBC; guidance reaffirmed at the Sep 17 Investor Day; $7.9B buyback authorization left [1-3]. The stock ($268) trades at ~11.7x FY27 EPS and ~9% SBC-adjusted FCF yield after a 62% one-year fall and a further ~23% drop in the past month [13,15]. Alternative-lane evidence is mixed. Negative: forum posters (Bogleheads) report switching to FreeTaxUSA on price [10], management's own admission that price is the top churn reason [14,15], several 2026 AI tax-agent launches [11,12], and the TurboTax app falling off the charts after the deadline (normal seasonality; that article is now gone (410) so I rely on the search snippet only) [9]. Similarweb shows September traffic down 11% m/m, which is off-season noise and does not move numbers [8]. Positive: Intuit is pushing through large QuickBooks price increases (Plus/Advanced ~+20-25% in Aug 2026 after a May wave) [5,6] while Xero is also raising prices from Oct 1 [7], which points to pricing power. Bookkeeper blogs note no documented migration wave and advise against switching on price alone [5,6]. The independent Substack case (~10x forward, $2B SBC, heavy buybacks) is plausible [4]. I found no prediction market relevant to INTU. X was not searched directly. Valuation: P/E $322 and FCF-yield $357 blend to ~$336. But I set the 12-month median at ~$290, below that fair value, because the disruption discount is unlikely to clear before real 2027 tax-season data and momentum is sharply negative. Distribution: lognormal around ~$290 with sigma ~0.45 (a little below the 50% realized vol, which was inflated by the crash), consistent with scenarios $180/$300/$430 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$303). Research was limited to ~15 queries; several claims from social or forum posts come from search snippets and are treated as sentiment only.
